narrative.overview: The songs are going into the car, so the interface speaks the language of Turkish highway signage. The one thing you must read first, the link field, sits on a fully saturated motorway-green sign with a white reflective border. Everything else is night asphalt: quiet, dark, and easy to scan. Signage is the only world the app borrows, and it supplies four things: type, palette, density and one signature move. Layout and controls stay ordinary web controls that any non-technical user already knows.
keyCharacteristics: One saturated sign field per job: green for input, blue for the active download.
A white reflective border inset from the field's edge, never a thin outline.
Overpass, from the Highway Gothic lineage, in heavy weights; tabular figures for every number.
Generous 64px controls for older, non-technical users.
Plain Turkish copy, never technical jargon.

rules.name: The Field Not Accent Rule
rules.body: Green and blue appear only as whole sign fields with the reflective border, never as a stray text colour or a thin stripe.

rules.name: The One Lit Sign Rule
rules.body: Only active downloads use Intercity Blue. When nothing is downloading, the only sign on screen is the green header.

rules.name: The Step Scale Rule
rules.body: Sizes come only from the fixed scale (0.8125 / 0.9375 / 1.0625 / 1.25 / 1.5 / 2 / 2.75rem). Never introduce an in-between size.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Percentages, times and counts always use tabular figures.

dos: Do give a new primary surface its own sign field with the reflective border.
Do keep every control at least 44px tall, and main actions at 56–64px.
Do write errors in plain Turkish that name the problem and what to do next.
Do use Lucide icons at a 2px stroke.
donts: Don't put a small label or kicker above a heading. Supplementary plates sit beside the heading.
Don't use green or blue as text colour or as thin side stripes.
Don't light more than the active rows in intercity blue.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons.
